what: Petrobras is Brazil's state-controlled oil company. It produces most of Brazil's oil, much of it from deepwater pre-salt fields that are among the cheapest large oil deposits in the world, and it refines and distributes fuel in Brazil.
customers: International oil buyers, Brazilian fuel distributors, refiners and petrochemical producers.
money: deepwater and pre-salt oil and gas production
moat: Pre-salt fields with extraction costs among the lowest in the industry and decades of reserves, in a country where it holds the dominant acreage position.
risks: The Brazilian government controls it and has in the past used fuel prices for political ends
Dividend policy can change with government priorities
Debt of about $71 billion remains substantial
Oil price swings move earnings directly
opportunities: Pre-salt production costs are so low that it earns money at oil prices where others do not
A dividend yield near 9% when oil prices are firm
Analysts see meaningful upside from current levels
watch: Pre-salt production growth and whether fuel pricing stays aligned with international prices.
